title: Distributive law
parts: a(b + c)
Multiply a by the sum inside the brackets
= ab + ac
which equals a times each term, added together.
note: Multiply every term inside the brackets.

title: Factorisation
parts: The difference of squares is written as a product of two factors.
note: Adding the factors does not reconstruct the expression. Multiply them.
wrong: The expression is the square of x−3.

title: Rational algebraic expression
parts: Cancelling the factor x−1 simplifies the fraction when x is not 1.
example: For x=3 the fraction is 8/2=4. At x=1 the original fraction is undefined.
note: Cancel common factors and preserve the original domain restriction.
wrong: Both expressions are defined and equal at x=1.

title: Binomial theorem
parts: (a+b)³ = a³ + 3a²b + 3ab² + b³
Expanding the cube gives terms whose coefficients are 1, 3, 3 and 1.
example: With a=2 and b=1, the expansion is 8+12+6+1=27.
note: The mixed terms come from choosing a or b from each factor.
wrong: Cube each term separately and add only a³ and b³.

title: Quadratic formula
parts: For ax²+bx+c=0 with a nonzero, use each sign to find the possible roots.
example: For x²−5x+6=0, the formula gives (5±1)/2, so x=2 or x=3.
note: Divide the entire numerator by 2a. If the square root is zero, the two signs give the same root.
wrong: Divide only the square root by 2a and then subtract b.

title: Simultaneous equations
parts: Find one pair of values that makes both equations true.
example: Adding the equations gives 2x=8, so x=4 and y=3.
note: A solution of just one of the equations does not solve the system.
wrong: Find any pair that satisfies either equation.

title: Inclusive inequality
parts: x is less than or equal to three.
example: The values 2.9 and 3 satisfy this inequality, but 3.1 does not.
note: The line under the angle includes equality.
wrong: x is strictly less than three.

title: Inequality under negative division
parts: Negative two times x is less than six,
so x > −3
so x is greater than negative three.
example: x=0 satisfies both statements, while x=−4 satisfies neither.
note: Multiplying or dividing an inequality by a negative number reverses its direction.

title: Absolute value inequality
parts: |x−a| < b
x lies less than b units from a.
note: Both endpoints are excluded because the inequality is strict.
wrong: All x to the left of a−b or right of a+b.

title: Polar form of a complex number
notation: z = r(cos θ + i sin θ)
parts: z = r(cos θ + i sin θ)
Write z using distance r from the origin and angle θ from the positive real axis.
note: r is the modulus of z. It is not the real part.
wrong: r is the real part and θ is the imaginary part.

title: De Moivre’s theorem
notation: (cos θ + i sin θ)ⁿ = cos(nθ) + i sin(nθ)
parts: (cos θ + i sin θ)ⁿ
Raising a unit complex number to an integer power n
= cos(nθ) + i sin(nθ)
multiplies its angle by n.
example: For θ=π/2 and n=2, the left side is i² and the right side is cos π+i sin π=−1.
note: Multiply the angle inside both trig functions.
wrong: Raise cos θ and i sin θ to power n separately and add them.
